title: Revolts Faraizi Revolt
definition: The Faraizi movement was a 19th-century socio-religious reform movement turned agrarian revolt, initiated by Haji Shariatullah in Eastern Bengal, aimed at purging Islamic practices of un-Islamic accretions and resisting the exploitation of peasants by British indigo planters and zamindars.
importanceInUpsc: It represents the transition of religious reform movements into militant peasant resistance, a recurring theme in UPSC Modern History questions regarding the nature of 19th-century anti-colonial struggles.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Revolts Faraizi Revolt.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Socio-religious reform movements in 19th century India
Permanent Settlement and its impact on Bengal peasantry
